Ms D.I. Charlewar, APP for respondent No.1/State.
Mr. Amit Bhate, counsel for respondent No.2.
Rule. Rule made returnable forthwith.

By consent of Mr. R.R. Maddalwar, counsel holding for Mr. A.M. Chandekar, learned counsel for applicants, Ms D.I. Charlewar, learned APP for non-applicant No.1/State and Mr. Amit Bhate, learned counsel for non-applicant No.2, the application is taken up for final hearing at the stage of admission.

2. By this application, the applicants are seeking quash and set aside Regular Criminal Case No.246 of 2022 arising out of Crime No. 82 of 2022 and Charge-sheet No.48 of 2022, registered for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 504 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The applicants herein are the husband, sister-in-law, mother- in-law, brother-in-law, niece, and nephew of the respondent No.2.

They approached this Court to challenge the registration of criminal proceedings against them on the ground that, even if the allegations which are levelled against them are accepted at their face value, the offence under Section 498-A IPC is not made out against the present applicants.
Therefore, they seek indulgence of this Court in the matter.
4. Learned APP has strongly opposed the present application.
According to the prosecution, there are specific allegations against the rkn 925apl920.2022.odt applicants that the complainant was not treated properly by the present applicants.

It is alleged that there was a demand of Rs.
50,00,000/-for purchasing a plot and for construction of a house, and for that purpose,
complainant
was subjected to mentally as well as physically tortured by the present applicants.

Hence, according to the prosecution, the offence is made out under Section 498-A and 504 IPC and therefore, at this stage, no indulgence of this Court is necessary in the matter.
5.
In the light of the submissions made by the learned Counsel for both sides before this Court, it would be relevant to consider Section 498-A of IPC.

The bare perusal of this provision shows that vide its Explanation -(a) the cruelty means any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of a woman.

As per Explanation - (b) harassment is done with a view to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
As such, while deciding these allegations, this Court has to first look into whether the cruelty which is allegedly falls in the explanation provided under Section 498-A of IPC or not.

6. It is also pertinent to note that the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and this Court has experienced that there is a tendency of implicating the husband and his relatives in the criminal offence on vague and omnibous allegations.

Therefore, this Court is required to be extremely careful Bipin Manoharrao Kathane And 5 Others vs State Of Mah. Thr. Rawanwadi Ps Gondia ... on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45298586/
2

sentences.text: and cautions in dealing with these complaints and must take pragmatic realities into consideration while dealing with matrimonial cases.
7. To attract the offence, it is necessary that the allegations levelled against the Applicant should be concrete and precise.

If it is found that the allegations are made without providing any specific details rkn 925apl920.2022.odt or describing any particular instance of harassment, in such cases,
where Informant did not mention date, time and place or manner in which the alleged harassment is occurred, the Court should be slow while holding that offence is made out against the applicants.

8. It is also held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the catena of cases that mere trivial irritations,
quarrels between spouses which happen in day-to-day married life not to be considered as cruelty.
The foundation of a sound marriage is tolerance, adjustment and respecting each other.

Therefore,
petty quibbles, trifling differences are general and should not be exaggerated and blown out of proportion to destroy the marriage.
9. After perusal of the entire record of the present application, it is pertinent to note that marriage of non-applicant No.2 with applicant No.1 was solemnized in the year 2010.

Out of the said wedlock,
they have two daughters.

The allegation is only that a demand of Rs. 50,00,000/- was made for purchasing a plot and construction of a house, and on that count, there was a harassment to the applicant.
10.
It is also pertinent to note that the allegations which are made are not specific and precise in nature.
There is no mention of date, time or the nature of allegations, nor it is stated in the application, as to how she caused harassment by the applicant.
The only vague and omnibus allegations are levelled against the present applicants.

11. In my opinion, to attract the rigor Section 498-A of IPC, the allegations must be of such a nature to fall within the ambit of "cruelty" as explained in clause (a) and (b) of Section 498-A of the IPC.

However, after going through entire record, no such serious allegations seems to be made against the present applicants in the matter.
12.
In my opinion, prima-facie the offence is not made out against the present applicants.
In view of the above reasons, I do not find it rkn 925apl920.2022.odt proper to allow continuation of criminal proceedings against the present applicants in the matter.
Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following order.
ORDER  a] The criminal application is allowed.

b] The proceedings bearing Charge-sheet No.48 of 2022,
pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gondia arising out of Crime No. 82 of 2022, for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 504 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, is hereby quashed Bipin Manoharrao Kathane And 5 Others vs State Of Mah. Thr. Rawanwadi Ps Gondia ... on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45298586/
3 and set aside.
